rv.q: Visually and audibly, Sayet's expertly written and performed theatrical memoir reminds us that history is no faraway thing, but a thriving part of the communities and nature that surround us, if only we pay attention.

Sayet is an engaging and restrained storyteller, fully in command of the stage for the full 80-minute running time — and aided by Hao Bai's simple but dramatic set design and Erik Schulke's understated sound design.

Sayet is more effective as a playwright than a performer, and the effort at a poetic effect in both Sayet's language and Mei Ann Teo's direction does not mask the gaps in the story that frames the play: Sayer's personal journey to England to study for a PhD in Shakespeare, which leads to her feeling betrayed.
